beats.text: Modular RAG shatters this bottleneck by decoupling retrieval into three distinct phases: pre-retrieval query expansion, precision in-retrieval fetching, and aggressive post-retrieval reranking.
beats.visual_focus: The monolithic pipeline snaps apart into three modular stages: Pre-Retrieval, In-Retrieval, and Post-Retrieval, each with dedicated filtering gates.

beats.text: Pre-retrieval rewrites ambiguous user queries for semantic precision, while post-retrieval compression prunes irrelevant context chunks before they ever pollute the transformer.
beats.visual_focus: A vague natural-language query morphs into an optimized multi-aspect vector, while downstream documents pass through a reranker and contextual compressor, discarding 80% of filler text.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: This hooked me right away—calling out LLMs hallucinating on proprietary data hits home because anyone building with LLMs runs into that immediately. Breaking RAG down into Pre, In, and Post retrieval with query rewriting and reranking makes the architecture click in 30 seconds without any corny baby-talk metaphors.

Everyone thought standard methods were enough, until RAG Survey proved: retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) refers to the retrieval of relevant information from external knowledge bases before answering questions with LLMs.
Your multi-billion parameter model still confidently hallucinates private facts the exact second its static training weights go stale.
Researchers just demonstrated an impressive 98.2% speedup using RAG Survey.

Why is RAG Survey a major breakthrough? Because large language models (LLMs) demonstrate powerful capabilities, but they still face challenges in practical applications, such as hallucinations, slow knowledge updates, and lack of transparency in answers.
